newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombia peso closes down amid real dollar demand.
newsitem.headline: Colombia peso closes down amid real dollar demand.

text.p: The Colombian peso closed down 4.5 at 1009.45 pesos to the dollar in the first session of 1997 as multinationals snapped up greenbacks, interbank traders said.

The presence of real demand spared the central bank from having to step in to prop up the dollar in order to forge ahead with its crawling peso devaluation, as it had been doing at the end of last year.
"Multinationals were looking for large quantities of dollars and that meant the central bank didn't have to step in and buy," one interbank trader said.
Dealers reported 318 trades worth a total $165.5 million. The peso hit an intraday high of 1,006.11 and an intraday low of 1,009.5
